question: A dyslipidemia with phenotype IIa of Fredrickson may have its origin in mutations in the gene of:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Mutations in the gene of the LDL receptor -> impaired clearance of LDL cholesterol -> dyslipidemia -> 95% CHAIN: Mutations in the gene of Lipoprotein lipase (LPL) -> reduced breakdown of triglycerides -> elevated levels of VLDL and chylomicrons -> dyslipidemia -> 90% CHAIN: Mutations in the gene of the Apo CII -> impaired activation of lipoprotein lipase -> reduced breakdown of triglyceride-rich lipoproteins -> dyslipidemia -> 85% CHAIN: Mutations in the gene of the Apo A-II -> altered function of HDL particles -> impaired reverse cholesterol transport -> dyslipidemia -> 80% CHAIN: Mutations in the gene of the Apo B-48 -> impaired chylomicron formation -> accumulation of chylomicron remnants -> dyslipidemia -> 95%
analysis: Dyslipidemia with phenotype IIa of Fredrickson is associated with elevated levels of low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol. Mutations in the gene of the LDL receptor can lead to impaired clearance of LDL cholesterol from the bloodstream, contributing to the development of this type of dyslipidemia.
